How do I apply?
Applicants may apply through the University of Loralai online admissions system. After completing the online application, download and print the form, attach all required documents along with the receipt of the application processing fee, and submit the complete hard copy to the Admissions Office. Please ensure that your application reaches the Admissions Office before the announced closing date.
What are the entry requirements?
Eligibility criteria vary by program. Applicants are advised to visit the relevant department webpage for detailed requirements.
What documents are required?
Applicants are required to submit the following documents along with their application:
Attested copy of Secondary School Certificate (SSC)
Attested copy of Higher Secondary School Certificate (HSSC)
Attested copy of the applicant’s CNIC / B-Form
Attested copy of local/domicile certificate
Bank draft, pay order, or receipt of cash payment (admission processing fee)
Six recent passport-size photographs
Attested copy of CNIC of the applicant’s father/guardian
Attested copy of character certificate from the last institution attended
What are the payment options?
Applicants are required to deposit the bank challan for the prospectus and application processing fee at any ABL branch, as per the following schedule:
DPT: Rs. 2000/-
BS Allied Sciences: Rs. 2000/-
BS: Rs. 1500/-

What is the duration of a program at UOLi?
Most BS programs are of four years’ duration, comprising eight semesters. However, the BS (DPT) program extends over five years, consisting of ten semesters. Each semester spans 18 weeks, including 16 weeks of instruction and two weeks allocated for midterm and final examinations. The standard duration for completion of an MS program is two years from the date of enrollment.
Can I change my program after admission?
Change of academic program is generally discouraged; however, it may be permitted within the first two weeks of the first semester, subject to the recommendation of the concerned Chairperson(s) and approval of the relevant Dean(s). Such a change is contingent upon fulfillment of the prescribed eligibility criteria, availability of seats, and the condition that the student’s merit must be higher than that of the last candidate admitted to the desired program.
Can I freeze a semester?

Can I freeze a semester?
Freezing of a semester is not permitted during the first semester of a program. However, after completion of the first semester, a student may apply to freeze for a maximum of two semesters over the entire duration of the program.

TO DISCUSS AND APPROVE THE ACADEMIC RULES FOR UNDERGRADUATE PROGRAMS, UNIVERSITY OF LORALAI
In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) (2) and (3) of Section 33 of the University of Loralai Act, 2012, the University with the approval of the Senate is pleased to make the following rules to regulate the under-graduate programs of studies of the University.
Preamble.
The Academic Rules for the Under-graduate program of studies offered by University of Loralai (UOLI) are in line with the guidelines provided by Higher Education Commission Pakistan regarding semester system. Aspects covered in these regulations include duration of undergraduate Programs; attendance, struck-offs, readmission; change of program; changing from one academic program to another; withdrawal and addition of courses; promotion & probation; freezing of a semester; course limit; examinations; award of degree; criterion for Gold Medal; repetition of courses for improvement of grades; conduct of summer sessions; maintenance of course files; migration / credit transfer policy; fee concession and award of scholarships; fee refund policy and discipline at campus.
Short title, commencement and application.
These rules may be called the University of Loralai (Under-graduate Programs of Studies) Rules, 2019.
These shall come into force at once.
Program of Study offered by UOLI

https://uoli.edu.pk/academic-rules__3666.content:
These shall come into force at once.
Program of Study offered by UOLI
The University of Loralai shall offer programs of studies as per its charter, needs in the job market, and on guidance of its statutory bodies from time to time.
The Program of studies offered shall have semester system of studies.
Duration of the Program
4.1 The programs leading to BS shall be of four years duration, equally divided into eight semesters.
4.2. Each semester shall be spread over eighteen weeks, 16 weeks for teaching, and two weeks for the preparation and the conduct of examinations.
Attendance, Struck offs and Readmission
Students shall have to be punctual and regular in attending all lectures, laboratory periods, semester sessions and fieldwork as required for each course.
Two weeks consecutive absence would result in a student’s name being struck off from the University rolls. Such a student must get himself/herself readmitted to the program within three (03) working days of the striking off of his/ her name on payment of readmission fee of Rs. 500/- and within further three (03) days on payment of readmission fee of Rs 1000/-. The failure on the part of a student in getting himself/ herself readmitted shall be considered as the cancellation of his/ her admission.

https://uoli.edu.pk/academic-rules__3004.content:
There shall be at the most three chances for readmission during the entire study program. A student readmitted 3 times during the entire study program shall not be allowed any further readmission and his/her admission shall stand canceled.
A student seeking readmission shall not be exempted from the payment of readmission fee.
Change of Program / Elective Courses
6.1 Changing from one academic program to another; change of academic program will be allowed on the recommendation of the chairpersons concerned and approval of the dean(s), within first two weeks of the first semester, subject to the fulfillment of eligibility criterion and availability of the seat. Merit of the student has to be above the merit of the last student admitted in the program to which transfer is desired.
Withdrawal and Addition of Courses
When a course, for which a student has enrolled, cannot be offered according to the announced program, the student may take an elective course. However, this must be done not later than 7 days after the date of enrollment.
A student, with the consent of chairperson of the department and on approval by the Dean, may be allowed to drop a course within 5 weeks of the commencement of semester.
Withdrawal from a course will be allowed, on the recommendations of the chairperson of the department and approval by the Dean, latest by the end of 15th week of the semester.
Withdrawal course will appear on the transcript with letter grade W

https://uoli.edu.pk/academic-rules__1171.content:
Withdrawal course will appear on the transcript with letter grade W
Courses withdrawn or dropped shall not account for calculation of GPA of the semester.
Promotion & Probationary Period
If a student scores CGPA less than 1.0 at the end of any semester during the program of studies, the student shall be dropped from the university rolls (GPA of first semester is CGPA as well).
Probation
Whenever any student’s CGPA falls between 1.0 and 2.0 he / she shall be put on the first probation list for the next semester
If the student fails to raise the CGPA to 2.0 or above, he/ she shall be placed on 2nd probation for the next semester.
If the student who was earlier on 2nd probation fails to raise CGPA to 2.0 or above, he/she shall be placed on the last probation.
If the student fails to raise CGPA to 2.0 or above in the last probation, he / she shall be dropped from the university rolls.
The student eligible to continue the study program and having failed in the course(s) shall repeat the course(s) whenever such course(s) shall be offered by the faculty provided the contents of the study program remain unchanged.
A student shall have to complete the BS Program within ten (10) semesters or five years (within twelve semesters.
Freezing of a Semester
No freezing in the first semester is allowed.
A student shall be allowed to apply for freezing of at the most two semesters in his / her entire program of studies.

https://uoli.edu.pk/academic-rules__2366.content:
A student shall be allowed to apply for freezing of at the most two semesters in his / her entire program of studies.
The case for freezing of the program shall be placed before the Vice Chancellor by the chairperson of the respective department through the Dean of the Faculty.
Being allowed a semester freeze by the Vice Chancellor, the student shall resume the program subject the commencement of the relevant semester. A student already registered shall not pay the registration / admission fee in order to resume the studies. However, the student has to complete the degree requirements within 5 years.
Course Limit
A student is required to take 15-18 credit hours course work per regular semester.
However the chairperson of the department may allow a maximum of 21 credit hour course work in one semester on the approval of the Dean.
Credit Hours
A credit hour means teaching a theory course for 50-60 minutes each week throughout the semester.
One credit hour in laboratory or experimental work would require lab contact of at least two hours per week throughout the semester
A course with 3 credit hours for theory and one credit hour for laboratory work will be denoted as 4 (3-1)
Examinations
Eligibility to Appear in the Final Examination of a Semester
No student shall be eligible to appear in the final examination unless he/she is registered at the University for the respective Study Program and has paid all the required dues.

https://uoli.edu.pk/academic-rules__5280.content:
A student must have attended at least 75% of the classes held in a course in order to be allowed to sit in the final semester examination.
Students having class attendance less than 75% in a particular course will be required to repeat the course when it is offered again.
A student must have submitted all assignments, term papers and reports in time before the commencement of the final semester examination.
Special Examination
A special examination shall be conducted for a student having failed to appear in an examination on medical grounds or the demise of parent, spouse, children and brother/sister.
A student must have met the eligibility criteria to appear in the respective examination of a semester
The student shall have to produce the death certificate of the kin referred to in 8.2.1 above.
A student shall have to submit an application of illness to the Dean of Faculty on or before the date of commencement of examination.
In case of serious illness of the student, he/she must have been hospitalized in a recognized private or a public sector hospital.
A student shall have to apply to appear in a special examination. The case shall be examined by the Departmental Committee and recommendations of the committee shall be placed before the Dean through the chairperson of the department for approval.
Special mid-semester examination: The student shall be allowed by the Dean to appear in special mid-semester examination to be
scheduled latest by the 12th week of the semester.

https://uoli.edu.pk/academic-rules__3615.content:
scheduled latest by the 12th week of the semester.
Special final semester examination: The student shall be allowed by the Dean to appear in the special final semester examination to take place during semester break before the commencement of next semester.
Chairperson of the Department will monitor the special examinations and ensure the standards.
There would be only one chance to appear in special examination during entire program of studies.
Departmental Committee
There shall be a “Departmental Committee” comprising:
Chairperson of the departments
Two seniors most faculty members
The committee will address the grievances of the students about any course instructor or grade or for any other academic issue.
Appellate body will be the Dean of the Faculty
Grievance on Grade
A student must approach the chairperson of the department for a grievance on grade within 5 days of the receipt of the grade.
The chairperson of the department shall forward the grade grievance to the “Departmental Committee”
It will be binding on the committee to hear both sides (student and instructor), and give the final decision within 5 days or before the start of the d ate of registration for the new semester whichever comes earlier
University Examination Committee
Constitution of the Committee
There shall be a University Examination Committee comprising of
Pro Vice Chancellor (Chairperson)
Registrar / his nominee
Deans of faculties

There shall be a University Examination Committee comprising of
Pro Vice Chancellor (Chairperson)
Registrar / his nominee
Deans of faculties
The Controller of Examinations will be the secretary of the University Examination Committee.
Functions of the University Examination Committee The committee shall
Have the mandate to permit and notify all the cases/ requests of special examinations after scrutiny of the evidence
Finalize the unfair means cases reported by examination committees of faculties
Monitor the mid and final semester examinations of faculties.
Faculty Examination Committee
There shall be a Faculty Examination Committee comprising of
Dean of Faculty
Chairpersons of Departments
One senior most faculty member
The teacher concerned may be co-opted in case of complaint of a student.
Functions of the Committee
Ensuring content coverage of courses by comparing tests with the course outlines and work plan provided by the teacher.
Monitoring of classroom activities as given in the course outline.
Examination of all problems regarding uniformity before the declaration of results.
Referring the special examination cases and the unfair means cases reported during mid semester and final semester examinations to the University Examination Committee.

Award of Degree
12.1 On successful completion of the examination, the controller of examinations of the University shall compile the final results of the study program and declare the results indicating the marks and grades obtained by the students.
The University shall confer the degrees upon the successful students.
Degree will not be awarded to a student whose CGPA is less than 2.0.
A student can repeat up to 18 credit hour courses with D grades for improvement of CGPA (if it is less than 2.0) in additional 9th and 10th semesters.
Criterion for Gold Medal Awards
Following is the criterion for award of gold medals to graduating students.
Highest CGPA in the program of studies
Successful completion of courses whenever initially offered during the program of studies
Completion of degree within minimum prescribed period
Immaculate character during studies
If the number of students, in a program of studies, is less than 10 then the minimum CGPA required for award of Gold Medal is 3.85

https://uoli.edu.pk/academic-rules__8336.content:
If the number of students, in a program of studies, is less than 10 then the minimum CGPA required for award of Gold Medal is 3.85
Repetition of Courses for the improvement of Grades
Any student failing in any course or debarred from taking the final examination on account of shortage of attendance shall have to repeat that course whenever offered.
A student who obtains a ‘D’ grade in a course may avail the opportunity of repeating that course whenever offered for improvement.
A student may repeat a maximum of six courses to improve D grades during entire program of studies.
In case a student repeats the course, the new improved grade for CGPA calculation will be substituted for the old grade in the official records.
Only one chance to repeat a course for the purpose of improvement for the entire degree program shall be allowed.
Students have to register for the courses being repeated within 10 days from the date of commencement of the semester.
The result of failed course(s) will be reflected in the transcript of respective semester(s) and in the subsequent semester(s) during which the failed course(s) was (were) passed.

Department of Allied Health Sciences
To become a recognized center of excellence in Allied Health Sciences by producing competent, ethical, and skilled healthcare professionals who contribute effectively to the healthcare system at national and international levels through quality education, clinical excellence, and research.
The mission of the Department of Allied Health Sciences, University of Loralai, is to provide quality, affordable, and accessible education in allied health disciplines, with a strong focus on academic excellence, professional training, ethical practice, community healthcare, and compliance with HEC and Allied Health Council standards.
Core Values
Academic Excellence
Affordability & Equity
Professional Ethics
Regulatory Compliance
Student Development
Innovation & Advancement
Community Service
Aims and Objective
The Department of Allied Health Sciences aims to:
Produce professionally competent graduates with strong theoretical knowledge and practical clinical skills.
Offer high-standard education with minimum tuition fees, ensuring accessibility as a public sector institution.
Promote ethical values, professionalism, and patient-centered care in all academic and clinical activities.
Encourage research, innovation, and continuous professional development in allied health sciences.
Contribute to the improvement of healthcare services, particularly in Balochistan and underserved regions.
Chairperson’s Message

Contribute to the improvement of healthcare services, particularly in Balochistan and underserved regions.
Chairperson’s Message
Welcome to the Department of Allied Health Sciences at the University of Loralai.
The University of Loralai is a public sector university committed to providing high-quality education in accordance with the standards and requirements set by the Allied Health Council and the Higher Education Commission (HEC) of Pakistan. Our department ensures that all academic and clinical programs meet national regulatory and professional benchmarks.
Currently, the Department of Allied Health Sciences is offering Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT), Anesthesia Technology, and Optometry. These programs are recognized as some of the most in-demand and highest-earning disciplines in the healthcare sector. Our curricula are designed to integrate strong theoretical foundations with hands-on clinical training, preparing graduates to excel in professional practice, research, and healthcare leadership roles.
Our dedicated and qualified faculty strive to create a dynamic learning environment that promotes academic excellence, ethical practice, and community service. We are committed to producing competent healthcare professionals who can contribute effectively to the national and international healthcare system.
I encourage our students to utilize the opportunities provided by the department and to pursue their academic journey with dedication, integrity, and professionalism.

Dr. Muhammad Ammar Lodhi (PT)
Chairperson, Department of Allied Health Sciences

Department of Commerce
To be the business school of Commerce for students, employers, businesses and stakeholders, that may lead to overcome the cutting-edge challenges of the contemporary business world.
In pursuit of excellence, offering innovative programs and high quality teaching in the field of commerce to prepare intellects with the competencies to offer practical solutions to industrial challenges. To prepare novel researchers adding conspicuous share in the globalization of the business world.
Core Values
Integrity
Compassion
Quality and Continuity
Students learning and development
Aims and Objective
The primary aim of the department is to produce skilled manpower for the developing economy of Pakistan. With this broad goal in view the following specific objectives have been laid down:
To prepare students for managerial career in government, commercial and industrial enterprises.
To prepare students for career in research and training institutions.
To undertake research on emerging issues in public and private enterprise.
To develop expertise on limited scale among the students by imparting knowledge in specialized fields.
Chairperson’s Message
Welcome to the Department of Commerce at University of Loralai! We are thrilled to introduce you to our dynamic and forward-thinking academic community, dedicated to nurturing future business leaders and professionals.

https://uoli.edu.pk/faculty/commerce__16.content:
As the Head of the Department of Commerce, I take great pride in the excellence of our faculty and the comprehensive program we offer. Our goal is to provide a holistic education that equips you with not only theoretical knowledge but also practical skills and real-world experience.
Here at Department of Commerce, we believe in fostering an inclusive learning environment that encourages innovation, critical thinking, and ethical decision-making. Our diverse faculty members are experts in their respective fields, and they are committed to supporting your academic journey and personal growth.
Choosing the right institution is a significant decision, and we understand the importance of finding the best fit for your educational journey. We invite you to explore our prospectus thoroughly and visit our campus to experience the vibrant academic atmosphere we offer.
Join us at the Department of Commerce, and together, let's embark on a transformative journey.
Mr. Adnan Ahmad Khan
Chairperson, Department of Commerce

Chairperson’s Message
Welcome to the Department of Computer Science at the University of Loralai.

Chairperson’s Message
Welcome to the Department of Computer Science at the University of Loralai.
In today's world, technology is not just a tool; it is the driving force behind progress. Here in Loralai, we are committed to empowering our students to become a part of this global change. Our mission is simple: to provide a strong foundation in the fundamentals of computing in a supportive and practical learning environment.
We focus on building your skills from the ground up—clear thinking, problem-solving, and hands-on experience with modern technologies. Our dedicated faculty is here to guide you, not just in your studies, but in shaping a successful career.
To our students, I say: Your journey here is about more than earning a degree. It is about building the confidence and ability to create solutions, to innovate, and to lead in the digital age. Whether you dream of developing software, securing networks, or launching your own tech venture, this department is your starting point.
We encourage you to learn with curiosity, work with passion, and aim to make a positive impact through technology. The future is digital, and together, we will prepare you to build it.
Mr. Ismail Khan
Chairperson, Department of Computer Science

Goals and Objectives of Department of Education
To produce good and well-oriented teachers and well equipped educational administrators, having firm and unshakeable faith in the everlasting principles and values of Islam as well as the cohesion and integrity of Pakistan as one unified nation. Educate students to read critically, write clearly and imaginatively, think logically,
Internationally recognized university contributing to the positive socio-economic and cultural development in Baluchistan and Pakistan, within the parameters of Islam
The Department of Education as one of the leading institutes in the region aims to produce quality education to cope up with future challenges, working for diversity and common good of all fellow humans.
The Department of Education provides supporting learning environment to prepare graduates with advanced knowledge and skills in pedagogy, educational leadership and management, research values the   growth of society. To impart quality education and produce highly qualified and trained teachers equipped with qualities of researcher, counselor, managers or administrators, assessment, technology-oriented experts, and leaders in education.
Core Values
1.To prepare teachers who can bring novelty and change.
2.To inculcate creativity and open-mindedness.
3.To pursue growth and creativity.

PROGRAM DESCRIPTION
This program offers a wider variety of the high-quality reading courses and builds deeper understanding of the advance techniques of qualitative as well as quantitative research. The goal of the PhD in Education program is to prepare the next generation of leading educational researchers. We anticipate that by active participation in the research of our faculty, students can develop the skill they need to undertake outstanding research of their own. Learning through a combination of theory and practice in various domains of educational enterprise, the students will be able to understand philosophical background of the knowledge construction and apply their knowledge in conducting research on the most important areas of their interest. The program will help students develop their skills to play their role as leaders, researchers, and policymakers, and to contribute to the discipline of education.

Department of Islamic Studies
To flourish under the guidance of the Qur’an and Sunnah as an informed, tolerant, enlightened, and intellectually refined society.
The mission of the Department of Islamic Studies is to help students understand the importance of religion in human life by providing quality education based on Islamic values, while developing critical and interpretive skills to address contemporary issues.
Core Values
Faith and Integrity
Knowledge and Research
Critical and Reflective Thinking
Inclusivity and Social Responsibility
Service to Society
Aims and Objective
To develop a comprehensive understanding of Islam and contemporary issues faced by the Muslim Ummah.
To cultivate the ability to transmit Islamic knowledge to future scholars.
To encourage and prepare female religious leadership.
To enhance critical thinking for religiously guided problem-solving.
To provide a sound foundation in core Islamic sciences.
To prepare students for advanced research in diverse fields of Islamic Studies.
Chairperson’s Message

To prepare students for advanced research in diverse fields of Islamic Studies.
Chairperson’s Message
The Department of Islamic Studies aspires to be recognized as a Center of Excellence by offering quality teaching and research through experienced and dedicated faculty members. The department emphasizes research-based knowledge derived from the Qur’an and Sunnah while remaining fully conscious of contemporary global challenges faced by the Muslim Ummah. Its academic programs combine foundational Islamic scholarship with critical thinking and moral development.

Department of Mathematics
To be a center of excellence in mathematical education and research, fostering analytical thinking and
innovation to solve real-world challenges.
The Department of Mathematics at the UOLi is dedicated to quality education, research excellence, and the development of critical thinking. We prepare students with strong mathematical foundations to contribute effectively to academic, scientific, and industrial advancement.
Core Values
Academic Excellence
Integrity & Ethics
Student-Centered Learning
Collaboration & Outreach
Inclusivity & Diversity
Problem-Solving & Critical Thinking
Aims and Objective
To provide high-quality education in mathematical sciences, equipping students with strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
To promote research and innovation in pure and applied mathematics, contributing to scientific and technological advancements.
To develop a critical thinking mindset among students, preparing them for careers in academia, industry, and research.
To bridge the educational gap in the region by offering accessible and competitive mathematics programs.
To foster collaborations with academic, industrial, and research institutions for knowledge exchange and professional growth.
Chairperson’s Message
Welcome to the Department of Mathematics at the University of Loralai, a hub of academic excellence and
research in mathematical sciences. Since its establishment in Fall 2019, the department has been committed

research in mathematical sciences. Since its establishment in Fall 2019, the department has been committed
to providing quality education and fostering a culture of innovation, critical thinking, and problem-solving.
Our highly qualified faculty, with strong academic and research backgrounds, is dedicated to equipping
students with the knowledge and skills necessary for success in academia, industry, and research. We take
pride in offering a rigorous BS Mathematics program that not only strengthens theoretical foundations but
also enhances analytical and computational abilities.
Located in Loralai, an underdeveloped region of Balochistan, our department plays a crucial role in bridging
the educational gap by offering students access to higher quality education. Despite challenges, we continue
to grow and strive for excellence in teaching and research. We are committed to developing a researchoriented academic environment where students are encouraged to explore new ideas, engage in mathematical
discoveries, and contribute to scientific advancements.
As we move forward, our goal is to expand academic programs, establish research collaborations, and provide
students with greater opportunities for intellectual and professional growth. I encourage all aspiring
mathematicians to join us on this journey of learning and discovery. Together, we can shape a brighter future
for mathematics and its applications in solving real-world problems.
Mr. Noor Ul Huda

Department of Pashto
To be a leading center for Pashto teaching and research, promoting Pashto heritage nationally and internationally, and producing graduates with strong linguistic and cultural understanding.
To deliver quality education and research in Pashto, preserve Pashtun heritage, promote modern scholarship, and prepare graduates for professional and academic fields.
Core Values
Academic Excellence
Cultural Preservation
Integrity and Ethics
Student Development
Aims and Objective
The primary aim of the department is to produce skilled, creative manpower for the developing literary culture of Pashto language. With this board goal in view the following specific objectives have been laid down.
To make students able for processing their learned information in Pashto literature and heritage.
To prepare students for analyzing Pashto classics and heritage in a scientific way.
To enable students for interpreting their day-dreams imaginations.
To discover new areas in Pashto literature.
Chairperson’s Message
Welcome to the Department of Pashto at the University of Loralai.
Learning in mother tongue is one of the key factors that have helped nations in finding place in list of developed nations. Pashto Department, in University of Loralai, efforts to keep Pashto language and Pashto literature in parallel with literatures of other languages. Moreover, Pashto department is on the mission of spreading knowledge of Pashto language and culture in forthcoming generation.

Department of Political Science
To be a leading center of excellence in political science education and research, fostering critical thinking, leadership, and policy innovation to address the unique socio-political and economic challenges of Balochistan and contribute to sustainable regional and national development.
The program delivers quality political science education while promoting research and leadership for effective participation in democratic governance and socio-economic development in Balochistan.
Core Values
Academic Excellence and Critical Inquiry
Democratic Engagement and Leadership
Regional Relevance and Social Responsibility
Aims and Objective
To provide high-quality political science education grounded in strong theoretical knowledge and practical skills.
To develop students’ critical thinking and analytical abilities for understanding political, social, and economic issues.
To promote research on governance, public policy, and conflict resolution relevant to Balochistan and Pakistan.
To prepare graduates for effective participation in democratic institutions and public service.
To cultivate ethical leadership, civic responsibility, and community engagement among students.
To strengthen collaboration with academic, governmental, and policy institutions at local, national, and international levels.
Chairperson’s Message

To strengthen collaboration with academic, governmental, and policy institutions at local, national, and international levels.
Chairperson’s Message
It is with great pride and enthusiasm that I welcome you to the Department of Political Science at the University of Loralai. Our department stands as a beacon of academic excellence, critical inquiry, and innovative research, deeply rooted in the dynamic sociopolitical landscape of Balochistan.
We are committed to providing a transformative educational experience that equips our students with the knowledge, analytical skills, and leadership qualities necessary to navigate and address the complex political and economic challenges facing our region and country. Our programs are designed to foster critical thinking, informed debate, and practical engagement with real-world issues, empowering our graduates to become responsible citizens, effective policymakers, and visionary leaders.
Recognizing the unique political and economic dynamics of Balochistan, our faculty and students actively engage in research that explores governance, conflict resolution, political economy, and sustainable development. We strive to contribute meaningful insights and solutions to the pressing challenges of our region through scholarly collaboration and community involvement.

I invite aspiring scholars and future leaders to join us in our mission to shape an inclusive, progressive, and prosperous society. Together, we can contribute to the political, social, and economic transformation of Balochistan and beyond.
Welcome to a journey of knowledge, leadership, and impact.
Mr. Abdul Baqi Khilji
Chairperson, Department of Political Science

Department of Zoology
To be a center of excellence in zoological sciences, producing skilled professionals and researchers who contribute to the understanding, conservation, and sustainable management of animal life and ecosystems through innovative research, education, and community engagement.
The Department of Zoology aims to provide quality education and research training to prepare students for biodiversity conservation, wildlife management, and ecological sustainability, while contributing to scientific advancement and environmental protection.
Core Values
Integrity
Compassion
Quality and Continuity
Student Learning and Development
Aims and Objective
The primary aim of the Department of Zoology is to produce skilled professionals who contribute to the fields of wildlife conservation, ecological research, and environmental sustainability. With this broad goal in mind, the following specific objectives have been outlined:
To prepare students for careers in wildlife conservation, environmental management, research institutions, and zoological organizations.
To equip students with scientific knowledge and practical skills necessary for conducting research in animal biology, biodiversity, and ecosystem sustainability.
To undertake research on emerging issues related to wildlife conservation, climate change, habitat preservation, and ecological balance.

https://uoli.edu.pk/faculty/zoology__781.content:
To undertake research on emerging issues related to wildlife conservation, climate change, habitat preservation, and ecological balance.
To develop expertise in specialized fields such as entomology, genetics, marine biology, and animal physiology, ensuring students gain in-depth knowledge and hands-on experience.
Chairperson’s Message
Welcome to the Department of Zoology at the University of Loralai! We are excited to introduce you to our vibrant academic community, dedicated to the study of animal life, biodiversity, and ecological conservation.
As the Head of the Department of Zoology, I take great pride in the excellence of our faculty and the well-structured programs we offer. Our aim is to provide a comprehensive education that combines theoretical knowledge with hands-on experience, preparing you for careers in research, wildlife conservation, and environmental sciences.
At the Department of Zoology, we foster an inclusive and innovative learning environment that encourages scientific inquiry, critical thinking, and ethical responsibility. Our distinguished faculty members, experts in their respective fields, are committed to guiding you through your academic and professional journey.
We look forward to supporting your aspirations and helping you make meaningful contributions to the field of zoology.
Ms. Salma Durrani

Office of Research, Innovation & Commercialization (ORIC)
In an era where knowledge defines progress, universities are no longer confined to teaching alone; they are engines of research, innovation, and socio-economic transformation. At the University of Loralai, the Office of Research, Innovation & Commercialization (ORIC) serves as the institutional backbone for nurturing a vibrant research culture and translating academic inquiry into meaningful societal impact.
Established in line with the policies and guidelines of the Higher Education Commission (HEC) of Pakistan, ORIC at the University of Loralai is committed to strengthening research excellence, fostering innovation, and enabling commercialization of knowledge. The office plays a pivotal role in empowering faculty members, researchers, and students to address regional and national challenges through impactful, ethical, and solution-oriented research.
Situated in a historically underserved region, ORIC recognizes its responsibility to align research with local needs while contributing to national development agendas. Through strategic collaboration with industry, government, and communities, ORIC aims to bridge the gap between theory and practice, ensuring that research outcomes lead to sustainable development, economic growth, and social well-being.
Message from the Director ORIC
Mr. Aslam Zaib
Welcome to the Office of Research, Innovation & Commercialization at the University of Loralai.

Mr. Aslam Zaib
Welcome to the Office of Research, Innovation & Commercialization at the University of Loralai.
Research and innovation are the foundations upon which progressive societies are built. At ORIC, University of Loralai, our vision extends beyond publications and projects—we aspire to create impact, empower ideas, and transform knowledge into solutions that matter.
Serving a region rich in potential yet facing unique challenges, we view research as a powerful tool for development, inclusion, and sustainability. Our commitment is to facilitate meaningful research that addresses real problems, strengthens industry linkages, and opens pathways for innovation and entrepreneurship.
ORIC is dedicated to supporting our faculty, researchers, and students by providing guidance, opportunities, and an enabling environment rooted in integrity and excellence. We encourage collaboration, creative thinking, and ethical research practices that align with national priorities and global standards.
Together, we aim to position the University of Loralai as a contributor to Pakistan’s knowledge economy and as a catalyst for positive change in Balochistan and beyond.
I invite all stakeholders to engage with ORIC and be part of this collective journey toward innovation, impact, and sustainable development.

News & Events
Vice Chancellor University of Loralai Represents Pakistan at SARCHE 2026
Vice Chancellor University of Loralai, Engr Prof. Dr. Ehsanullah Kakar Participates in SARCHE 2026, Dhaka, Bangladesh
Visionary leadership in higher education is shaped through global engagement, regional collaboration, and informed participation in policy discourse. Reflecting this commitment, the University of Loralai was honored to represent Pakistan at the South Asian Regional Conference on the State of Higher Education and Future Pathway (SARCHE 2026), held at Hotel Le Méridien, Dhaka, Bangladesh, through the participation of its Vice Chancellor, Engr. Prof. Dr. Ehsanullah Kakar.
The prestigious high-level regional conference was jointly organized by the University Grants Commission (UGC) of Bangladesh and the World Bank, bringing together senior policymakers, Vice Chancellors, rectors, higher education leaders, and international researchers from across South Asia and beyond. The conference focused on strategic reforms, governance innovation, digital transformation, and future pathways for strengthening higher education systems in the region.

The inaugural session was graced by the Honorable Chief Adviser as the Chief Guest, while the Honorable Education Adviser and Education Secretary attended as Special Guests. The welcome address was delivered by UGC Member Professor Dr. Tanjim Uddin Khan, and the session was chaired by the Honorable Chairman, University Grants Commission (UGC), Bangladesh. Nearly two hundred Vice Chancellors and senior academic leaders from home and abroad participated in the conference.
Representing Pakistan alongside other distinguished national leaders, Engr. Prof. Dr. Ehsanullah Kakar, Vice Chancellor University of Loralai, participated as part of a high-profile Pakistani delegation that included:
Dr. Farid, Member, HEC Commission
Prof. Dr. Arbella Bhutto, Vice Chancellor, SABS University
Dr. Zia-ul-Haq, Executive Director, HEC
Mr. Syed Naveed Shah, Director (M&E), HEC
Gen. Shahid Kiani, Rector, NUML
Dr. Raheel Qamar, Rector, COMSATS University
The participation of the Vice Chancellor of the University of Loralai at this eminent international forum underscores the growing regional and international recognition of the University and reflects its strong commitment to academic leadership, policy engagement, and cross-border collaboration in higher education.

The University of Loralai takes pride in being part of this important regional dialogue and reaffirms its resolve to contribute meaningfully to higher education reforms while aligning institutional development with emerging global best practices.

News & Events
NDMA–Universities Alliance for Disaster Resilience
Engr. Prof. Dr. Ehsanullah Kakar, Vice Chancellor of the University of Loralai, together with delegations from Balochistan’s public universities, signed a Letter of Agreement with NDMA to strengthen disaster risk reduction and management.
The agreement will establish NDMA Hubs and Centers of Excellence at participating universities to promote research, training, and skilled human resources for Balochistan’s unique disaster challenges.
“This collaboration will ensure locally relevant, evidence-based, and sustainable disaster management solutions,” said Engr. Prof. Dr. Ehsanullah Kakar.
Air Commodore Tanvir Paracha, NDMA Executive Director, added: “Universities are key to building resilience and developing the next generation of disaster management professionals.”
The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) has entered into strategic collaboration with leading public sector universities to promote climate resilience and disaster risk reduction across Pakistan, with a special focus on Balochistan. The collaboration was formalized through the signing of Letters of Agreement (LoAs), marking an important step towards evidence-based, anticipatory, and proactive disaster management.

The University of Loralai was represented by the Worthy Vice Chancellor, Engr. Prof. Dr. Ehsanullah Kakar, alongside Vice Chancellors and senior representatives of other distinguished universities of Balochistan and Punjab. The participating institutions included Sardar Bahadur Khan Women’s University, University of Balochistan, BUITEMS Quetta, LUAWMS Uthal, Mir Chakar Khan Rind University Sibi, University of Makran Panjgur, University of Turbat, BUET Khuzdar, University of Gwadar, Bolan University of Medical & Health Sciences Quetta, and Superior University Lahore.
During the engagement, the university leadership appreciated NDMA’s transition from reactive emergency response to a risk-informed and anticipatory governance model, particularly its advanced early warning systems and hazard forecasting mechanisms at the National Emergencies Operations Centre (NEOC). The Vice Chancellors also emphasized the importance of establishing regional and subject-specific Centers of Excellence to further strengthen research, training, and policy support in climate change and disaster management.
This collaboration reflects a shared commitment to transforming academic knowledge into practical solutions for building a safer and more resilient Pakistan.

UoL Strengthens Teachers’ Professional Skills
6-Day Teachers Training Workshop Conducted at the University of Loralai
Commanding Officer Loralai Scouts, Brigadier Noman Nazeer, and the Worthy Vice Chancellor of the University of Loralai, Engr. Prof. Dr. Ehsanullah Kakar, appreciated the successful completion of a six-day Teachers Training Workshop conducted by the University of Loralai in collaboration with Loralai Scouts.
The Teachers Training Workshop was held from 11 December to 16 December and was attended by teachers from various schools and colleges of District Loralai. The workshop focused on strengthening teaching methodologies, classroom management, and professional skills.
The workshop was organized by the Directorate of ORIC in collaboration with the Department of Education, University of Loralai. The Worthy Vice Chancellor, Engr. Prof. Dr. Ehsanullah Kakar, reaffirmed the university’s commitment to capacity building and community-oriented educational initiatives.
Brigadier Noman Nazeer commended the collaborative efforts and emphasized the importance of continuous professional development for teachers to improve educational outcomes in the region.
Special appreciation is extended to Mr. Aslam Zaib, Director ORIC, and the trainers from the Department of Education, University of Loralai, for their dedication, professionalism, and effective delivery of the training sessions, which ensured the success of the workshop.
The University of Loralai remains steadfast in promoting academic excellence and strengthening partnerships for the betterment of education in the region.

UoL Signs MoU with Pakistan Bait-ul-Mal
Under the leadership of the Worthy Vice Chancellor, University of Loralai, Engr. Prof. Dr. Ehsanullah Kakar, and with the valued support and encouragement of the Honorable Governor of Balochistan, Mr. Jaffar Khan Mandokhail, the University of Loralai signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Pakistan Bait-ul-Mal (PBM) on December 11, 2025, to support talented and underprivileged students through educational stipends and academic assistance.

UoL Participates in 7th National Olive Gala
The University of Loralai participated with distinction in the 7th Grand National Olive Gala 2025, held from 12 to 14 December 2025 at F-9 Park, Islamabad. Organized by the Ministry of National Food Security & Research (MNFSR), Government of Pakistan, this premier national event adopted the theme: “Promotion of Olive Cultivation on Commercial Scale in Pakistan – Phase II.”
The gala was inaugurated by the Federal Minister for National Food Security & Research, Mr. Rana Tanveer Hussain, convening farmers, entrepreneurs, researchers, policymakers, and industry leaders from across Pakistan.
The University of Loralai’s exhibit underscored its dedication to advancing olive cultivation, processing, and value-added products through cutting-edge research, innovation, and academic programs. The stall highlighted the exemplary contributions of Dr. Shafiq Ur Rehman, Focal Person for the Olive Project, with essential support from Assistant Professor Dr. Tariq Khan.
The University extends profound gratitude to the Worthy Vice Chancellor, Engr. Prof. Dr. Ehsanullah Kakar, whose visionary leadership has established and fortified olive initiatives—fostering future income generation, regional development, and excellence in agricultural studies.

This landmark event enjoyed robust support from national and international partners, including the Pak Olive Project, OliveCulture II, Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS), CIHEAM Bari, HHRD, PPAF, and FACE, reinforcing collaborative efforts for a sustainable agricultural future in Pakistan.
Together, we advance innovation, sustainability, and self-reliance in agriculture.

Major Step in Clinical Education at UoL
The Department of Allied Health Sciences, in collaboration with the Quality Enhancement Cell (QEC) and the Office of Research, Innovation & Commercialization (ORIC), has successfully initiated clinical rotations for Physical Therapy and Anesthesia Technology students (Batch Spring 2024) at ARIA Institute of Medical Sciences, Quetta.
During the visit, students were facilitated with a comprehensive and informative clinical orientation by Dr. Arsalan Ansari and Dr. Ammar Lodhi, who introduced them to various hospital departments, clinical protocols, patient management systems, and professional responsibilities.
This valuable clinical exposure significantly enhanced students’ understanding of real-world healthcare environments, promoting hands-on learning, professional development, and clinical competence.
Such collaborative initiatives reflect the University of Loralai’s continued commitment to academic excellence, quality assurance, and outcome-based clinical training for future healthcare professionals.

# PREE UoLi
Program Review for Effectiveness and Enhancement (PREE)
Introduction to PREE
Program Review for Effectiveness and Enhancement (PREE) is a comprehensive quality 
assurance mechanism developed by the Quality Assurance Agency (QAA) of Pakistan, in 
collaboration with QAA-UK, as part of the Revamped Quality Assurance Framework (PSG-
2023). PREE aims to evaluate and enhance the quality of academic programs at higher education 
institutions (HEIs) in Pakistan, ensuring they meet both international benchmarks and local 
contextual needs. It serves dual purposes: providing accountability to stakeholders (students, 
employers, and the public) and fostering continuous improvement in higher education.
PREE is designed to assess programs at the graduate level (Levels 7 and 8 of the National 
Qualifications Framework of Pakistan) and operates through structured internal and external 
review processes. It promotes a “quality culture” within HEIs by integrating self-assessment and 
external evaluation, focusing on program effectiveness, student learning experiences, and 
academic standards.
Types of PREE
PREE is implemented in two distinct but complementary forms, each targeting a specific aspect 
of quality assurance at the program level:
PREE for Internal Quality Assurance (PREE for IQA)
Description: This is a self-assessment process conducted by the academic program within an 
HEI. It encourages program to evaluate their performance against predefined PREE standards,

[PREE UoLi — continued]
HEI. It encourages program to evaluate their performance against predefined PREE standards, 
fostering a culture of self-reflection and improvement.
Purpose: To ensure programs internally monitor and enhance their quality, aligning with 
institutional goals and the Quality Assurance Framework.
Process: Involves a program team preparing a Self-Assessment Report (SAR), overseen by the 
Institutional Quality Assessment and Effectiveness (IQAE) office, with steps including evidence 
collection, action planning, and follow-up monitoring.
Frequency: Conducted routinely, typically annually or as per the assessment cycle determined 
by the institution.

[PREE UoLi — continued]
PREE for External Quality Assurance (PREE for EQA)
Description: This is an external review process managed by QAA, involving a panel of peer 
reviewers who assess graduate-level programs (Levels 7-8) against PREE Standards and 
Accreditation Council criteria.
Purpose: To provide an independent evaluation of program quality and standards, ensuring 
accountability and informing the public while encouraging enhancement.
Process: Includes submission of a program self-assessment document, a student submission, 
desk-based analysis by the review panel, an on-site visit, and a final report with outcomes such 
as “approved,” “approved with conditions,” or “not approved.”
Summary of PREE Standards
The PREE Standards are the core criteria against which programs are assessed under both 
PREE for IQA and PREE for EQA. These standards, outlined in the Quality Assurance 
Framework, ensure consistency and quality across academic programs. Below are the eight 
PREE Standards.

[PREE UoLi — continued]
Standard 1: Program Mission, Objectives, and Outcomes
Focus: Ensures the program has a clear mission aligned with institutional goals and defines 
measurable objectives and learning outcomes.
Expectation: Programs articulate their purpose and ensure outcomes meet academic and 
professional standards.
Standard 2: Curriculum Design and Organization
Focus: Evaluates the structure, coherence, and relevance of the curriculum to ensure it supports 
intended learning outcomes.
Expectation: Curriculum is well-designed, up-to-date, and aligned with national and 
international benchmarks.
Standard 3: Subject-Specific Facilities
Focus: Assesses the availability and adequacy of facilities (e.g., labs, libraries) specific to the 
program’s discipline.
Expectation: Resources are sufficient and accessible to support teaching and learning 
effectively.
Standard 4: Student Advising and Counselling
Focus: Ensures robust support systems for student guidance, including academic advising and 
personal counseling.
Expectation: Students receive adequate support to succeed academically and personally.
Standard 5: Teaching Faculty/Staff
Focus: Evaluates the qualifications, expertise, and performance of faculty and staff delivering 
the program.
Expectation: Faculty are competent, trained, and sufficient in number to meet program needs.

[PREE UoLi — continued]
Standard 6: Institutional Policies and Process Control
Focus: Reviews the policies and processes governing program delivery, including quality 
assurance mechanisms.
Expectation: Clear, effective policies ensure consistent program management and improvement.
Standard 7: Institutional Support and Facilities
Focus: Assesses broader institutional resources (e.g., IT, libraries, study spaces) supporting the 
program.
Expectation: Institutions provide comprehensive support to enhance the student learning 
experience.
Standard 8: Institutional General Requirements
Focus: Ensures a research-conducive environment for graduate programs, particularly research 
degrees, with attention to supervision, facilities, and outcomes.
Expectation: Programs maintain a high-quality research environment aligned with academic and 
societal needs.
Significance of implementing PREE
PREE integrates global best practices with local solutions, making it a tailored framework for 
Pakistan’s diverse higher education sector. By addressing both internal self-assessment (IQA) 
and external validation (EQA), it ensures program are effective, student-centered, and aligned 
with national and international standards. The eight PREE Standards provide a robust foundation 
for evaluating and enhancing academic quality, ultimately unlocking the potential for 
transforming higher education in Pakistan.

# UoLi Harrassment Policy
UNIVERSITY OF LORALAI : HARASSMENT POLICY
(To be read in conjunction with HEC Anti-Harassment Policy 2023)
 Introduction
University of Loralai is committed to provide plausible anti-harassment procedures to all students,
faculty, and staff to provide a conducive, dignified, and comfortable working environment where 
human rights and privileges are protected with equity, dignity, and safety. Policy is developed with 
particular focus on female gender based on our religion and cultural norms; however, no gender 
discrimination or gender equality is compromised. 
 
 Harassment has different tears, ranging from undesirable and aggressive behaviour to physical
assault, which disturbs the conducive working environment in the university. These can be triggered 
by students, faculty, staff, and vendors intending to humiliate others using different mediums –
physical, verbal or electronic (using IT devices).
University of Loralai will have “zero tolerance” on this aspect. It will make an utmost endeavour
to protect all human resources from any harassment to restore the reputation of the institution and 
identify culprits for definite punitive actions. Harassment is categorised as under: 
 
 Physical Harassment includes violence, both physically or to property and other types of physical
abuse. 
 Personal Harassment, also called bullying, involves unwanted remarks, insults, offensive and
derogatory statements, and constantly putting someone down with derogatory comments.

[UoLi Harrassment Policy — continued]
derogatory statements, and constantly putting someone down with derogatory comments. 
 Discriminatory Harassment is directed at someone’s gender, age, caste, ethnicity, religious sect,
lifestyle, or another form of a protected class who is subjected to offensive or intimidating remarks. 
 Psychological Harassment: The victim is often put down, belittled, or has to listen to needless
condescending remarks (both at professional and personal levels) that can affect their 
psychological well-being or mental health. These negative remarks can be aimed at the victim. 
 Cyberbullying is done online and involves threatening statements, rumours, and fake news
against the victim and making one’s confidential data (whether natural or forged) viral on social 
media to harm their mental health, personal reputation, and integrity. 
 Sexual Harassment is when the offender behaves romantically or sexually towards the victim,
who is uncomfortable and does not want attention of this nature. There is also something known 
as Quid Pro Quo sexual harassment, where the superior makes a sexual request or advancement to 
the victim and, upon refusal, threatens the victim of losing their grades, job, or the chance of 
promotion. It is incredibly offensive when the authorities make such submissions a condition 
towards any University activity or benefit. 
 3rd Party Harassment comes from someone not a permanent member of the University of Loralai

[UoLi Harrassment Policy — continued]
towards any University activity or benefit. 
 3rd Party Harassment comes from someone not a permanent member of the University of Loralai
community. These can include vendors, contractors, visiting faculty members, etc. There are still 
other forms, such as verbal harassment, power harassment, and retaliatory harassment. All of 
this contributes to a toxic and hostile workplace.
 Aim: To prevent all acts of harassment from the workplace to act upon complaints, to take punitive
actions promptly, reasonably, professionally and with full justice to the involved persons, and to 
ensure the confidentiality of all parties as a corollary course.

[UoLi Harrassment Policy — continued]
 Applicability: This policy applies to University students, staff and faculty working at Main, sub-
campuses, and affiliate colleges. This policy also applies to other members of the University of 
Loralai community, such as interns, hostilities, etc.; visiting personnel in an official capacity; 
and third parties, such as vendors, service providers, visitors, etc. The jurisdiction of this policy 
also encompasses University of Loralai computing or network resources accessed from an off-
campus location, which shall be deemed to have occurred on campus. This policy covers all types 
of harassment, as mentioned above.
## UoLi Harrassment Policy — 1. Preventing Harassment: Precautions for Different Types

## UoLi Harrassment Policy — 1. Physical Harassment:
Precautions:
i. Respect Personal Space: Always maintain a respectful physical distance from others,
especially if you're unfamiliar with them.
ii. Seek Consent for Physical Contact: Obtain explicit and voluntary consent before initiating
physical contact, such as handshakes or hugs.
iii. Mind Body Language: Be mindful of your body language. Avoid aggressive or invasive
gestures, and ensure your physical presence is non- threatening.

## UoLi Harrassment Policy — 2. Personal Harassment
Precautions:
i. 
Respect Privacy: Refrain from prying into someone's personal life or invading their personal
space, belongings, or information.
ii. 
Confidentiality: Maintain confidentiality by not sharing personal details or private information
about others without explicit consent.
iii. 
 Listen Actively: Actively listen when someone expresses discomfort, the need for privacy, or a
desire to set personal boundaries. Respect their wishes.

## UoLi Harrassment Policy — 3. Discriminatory Harassment
Precautions
iv. 
Celebrate Diversity: Embrace diversity and respect individuals from all backgrounds,
avoiding stereotypes, biases, and discriminatory behaviour.
v. 
Educate Yourself: Make an effort to educate yourself about different cultures, backgrounds,
and perspectives to foster an inclusive environment.
vi. Speak Up Against Discrimination: If you witness discrimination or biased behaviour,
stand up for the person facing it and report such incidents.

## UoLi Harrassment Policy — 4. Psychological Harassment
Precautions
a. Mind Your Words: Use language that is respectful, inclusive, and sensitive to others' feelings
and experiences.
b. Avoid Emotional Manipulation: Refrain from emotional manipulation, bullying, or any
behaviour harming someone's emotional well-being.
c. 
Seek Consent for Sensitive Conversations: When discussing sensitive or personal topics,
seek consent and respect boundaries.

## UoLi Harrassment Policy — 5. Cyberbullying
Precautions
a. Respect Online Boundaries: Do not invade someone's online privacy, engage in online
harassment, or participate in cyberbullying.
b. Think Before Posting: Be considerate of the content you post online, thinking about how it
might impact others.
c. Report and Support: If you witness cyberbullying or online harassment, report it and
support the victim.

## UoLi Harrassment Policy — 6. Sexual Harassment
Precautions
a. Prioritize Consent: In any intimate or personal relationship, always obtain explicit and
voluntary consent from all parties involved.
b. Avoid Unwanted Advances: Refrain from making unwanted sexual advances, comments, or
engaging in inappropriate behaviour.
c. Respect Boundaries: Respect the personal boundaries of others and their right to say no at
any time.

## UoLi Harrassment Policy — 7. Third-Party Harassment
Precautions
a. Intervene and Report: If you witness someone being harassed by a third party, consider
intervening if it's safe and appropriate. Report the incident to the relevant authorities.
b. Provide Support: Offer support and resources to the victim and encourage them to report
the harassment.
By adhering to these specific precautions, individuals can help create a respectful, inclusive, and
harassment-free environment within the university community. Understanding and following

these guidelines is essential to prevent all forms of harassment, whether intentional or
unintentional.

## UoLi Harrassment Policy — 8. Designated Resources
a. The University of Loralai shall designate at least two members of the administration, preferably
females, as the “Focal Persons” – one representing the directorate of Student Affairs and 
Registrar office – to offer support and immediate assistance to all such students as well as the 
employees, who have experienced harassment of any nature. Contact information of such 
individuals shall be readily available, including the University website. 
b. The University of Loralai shall also constitute a sexual Harassment Inquiry Committee to
investigate and adjudicate any allegations of prohibited conduct by the policy. 
c. Those who have experienced sexual harassment may also contact members of the Inquiry
Committee for support and advice.

## UoLi Harrassment Policy — 9. Complaints and Reporting
a. A complaint may be lodged by any person who has experienced harassment with the Focal
Persons, proctors, or any member of the respective Inquiry Committees, including the Sexual 
Harassment Committee. 
 
b. University of Loralai Students are encouraged to file their written complaints through the
Student Affairs directorate. University employees are advised to report their harassment 
complaints in written form to the Registrar office. 
 
c. Upon receiving any harassment complaint, the focal persons (at registrar and from Student
Affairs) will evaluate the nature of the complaint to identify and categorise it from the types of 
harassment. Where required, input from the registrar may also be sought to identify the 
harassment category.
d. Initial reporting of the complaints shall be done in the following ways:
 All the reported cases, whatever category they may fall into, shall be notified to the Vice
Chancellor and the Registrar. 
 If an University student files a personal, physical, or psychological harassment complaint
(which includes bullying, physical fight, or mental torture, etc.) against another University 
student, the proctors at the Directorate of Student Affairs shall forward it to the University 
Disciplinary Committee, which will complete its due process within 48 hours. 
 If an University student files a personal, physical, or psychological harassment complaint
against some University staff or faculty member, the case will be forwarded to the Grievance

 If a complainant is reluctant to contact the Focal Persons or any members of the Inquiry

 All members of the University community are encouraged to report any instances of sexual

 As soon as a complaint or report is received by one of the designated resources, it shall be shared

 For minor violations, complainants may opt to make an informal complaint to either the Focal

## UoLi Harrassment Policy — 10. Inquiry Committees
The Vice-Chancellor constitutes the following types of Committees to investigate harassment 
cases of varying natures at University of Loralai:
a. 
Disciplinary Committee for handling bullying or personal, physical, or even 
psychological harassment cases of University students towards their peers and teachers. 
b. 
Grievance Redressal Committee for handling bullying or personal, physical, 
discriminatory, or even psychological harassment cases of University employees. 
c. 
Harassment Inquiry Committee to handle sexual harassment cases of University 
students, staff or faculty members. 
d. 
Grievance Redressal Committee to handle discriminatory cases of University students 
against their teachers, supervisors or HoDs.
The respective Inquiry Committees shall be responsible for the investigation and adjudication of 
any complaint, including those of sexual harassment, received in connection with the violation 
of this policy.

## UoLi Harrassment Policy — 11. Harassment Inquiry Committee
The constitution of the Harassment Inquiry Committee is as follows:
a. 
The committee shall consist of three members, at least one of whom shall be a female, 
and one of the members shall be a member of the senior management of University. 
b. 
All members of the committee shall be University employees and will be appointed by the 
Vice- Chancellor. 
c. 
Members of the Committee shall be individuals known for being moral, credible, fair, 
gender-sensitive and strong-minded (someone who will not change their decision due to 
pressure from friends, colleagues or seniors). They shall have no conflict of interest in 
particular cases and be impartial and unbiased. 
d. 
Members of the Committee shall be appointed for two years (shorter terms may be 
required occasionally to fill vacancies). No member shall serve for more than two 
consecutive terms. Former members will be eligible for reappointment after a lapse of 
two years. 
e. 
One of the members of the committee shall be appointed as the Chair by the VC, whose 
duties shall include, but are not limited to, the following: maintaining order during 
hearings, answering procedural questions, granting or denying adjournments, 
maintaining proper documentation of the proceedings which shall constitute the official 
record, and reporting recommendations of the Committee to the VC. All these duties 
shall be undertaken in consultation with the Committee members. 
f.

shall be undertaken in consultation with the Committee members. 
f. 
If a complaint is made against one of the committee members, that member shall be 
replaced by another (impartial member) for that particular case. 
g. 
The University shall endeavour to train members of the Inquiry Committee in the 
investigation and adjudication of conduct prohibited under this policy. 
h. 
An University staff member shall be appointed to assist the Inquiry Committee. This work 
shall include responsibilities such as organising meetings, acting as a liaison between the 
committee and the other parties involved, keeping records, making and updating a 
database to track the processing of complaints, and ensuring appropriate awareness- 
raising about the issue of sexual harassment at University.

## UoLi Harrassment Policy — 9. Parental Notification
9.1. In cases where the victim is a student, and the focal person at the Directorate of Student 
Affairs finds it appropriate to inform or involve their parents at any stage of the case 
proceedings, the victim's consent will be sought. The parents will be notified carefully and 
inappropriately through the Directorate of Student Affairs.
9.2. In cases where the respondent is a student, their parents shall be duly notified of the case 
findings either through the Directorate of Student Affairs or the office of the Registrar.

## UoLi Harrassment Policy — 10. Right of Appeal
10.1. Both the complainant and the respondent shall have a right to appeal against the decision 
of the Inquiry Committee within 15 days from the date of notification.
10.2. In The cases in which the conduct falls within the scope of the University Act, the aggrieved 
party shall have the option to file an appeal to the Ombudsman by the provisions of the 
2010 Act.
10.3. There shall be a three-member appellate body (the “Appellate Body”) appointed by the VC 
– that shall include at least one senior member of the University administration (at the level 
of dean, director or equivalent) and at least one female members from the faculty. No

metadata.section: UoLi Harrassment Policy — 10. Right of Appeal

https://uoli.edu.pk/wp-content/uploads/2.content:
[UoLi Harrassment Policy — 10. Right of Appeal — continued]
member of the Inquiry Committee shall concurrently be a member of the Appellate Body. 
If the complaint had been made against one of the committee members, that member shall 
be replaced by another (impartial member) for that particular case. 
10.4. Appeal to the Appellate Body against the decision of the Inquiry Committee can be filed 
on the following grounds: 
 The alleged conduct does or does not fall within the scope of this policy.
 The Inquiry Committee decided without consideration of material information. 
 The imposed penalty is unfair because it is disproportionate or materially different from
that imposed for similar misconduct or 
 The adjudication process followed by the Committee was procedurally unfair.
10.5. 
To reach its decision, the Appellate Body may communicate with the parties, the members 
of the Inquiry Committee or other members of the University community as it deems fit.

## Anti Drug Policy For Higher Education Institutions In Pakistan — 1. Overview
Drug abuse poses serious risk to human health. According to a report titled, ‘Global Burden
of Disease’, around the world there were 585,000 deaths and 42 million years of “healthy” life lost
as a result of the use of drugs1. Substance use disorders constitute public health problems,
developmental issues and security hazards, both in industrialized and developing countries
worldwide. Prevention and treatment of drug use disorders are essential demand reduction
strategies of significant importance for public health.
Despite wide acknowledgment of its risks to human health and social life, drug abuse is on
the rise. The trend of drug consumption has become rampant amongst the youth of our country.
According to the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime report on ‘Drug use in Pakistan
2013’2, about 6.7 million people aged 15-64 were exposed to drugs. Among these, 4.25 million
people were estimated to be drug-dependent (addicts). The survey further revealed that cannabis
was the most commonly used drug, with around 4 million users nationwide. Around 0.86 million
people consumed heroin regularly, approximately 19,000 people reported that they had
experimented with ‘Ice’ (methamphetamine) and nearly 1.6 million people reported the misuse of
prescription opioids (painkillers) for non-medical use. Poly drug use was also common, with one
in five reporting combining drugs. Of all the people who reported drug consumption, 78% were

metadata.section: Anti Drug Policy For Higher Education Institutions In Pakistan — 1. Overview

https://uoli.edu.pk/wp-content/uploads/2.content:
[Anti Drug Policy For Higher Education Institutions In Pakistan — 1. Overview — continued]
in five reporting combining drugs. Of all the people who reported drug consumption, 78% were
men and 22% were women. Women were found to predominantly use tranquilizers, sedatives and
artificial stimulants (amphetamines).
These statistics reflect that a large number of people (both men and women) in Pakistan
have succumbed to drug addiction and the first exposure to this malady is usually at the latter half
of the teenage. It can also be inferred that if these youngsters are made aware of the consequences
and repercussions of drug abuse, there is a chance that the coming generations could be saved from
this problem.

## Anti Drug Policy For Higher Education Institutions In Pakistan — 2. Smoking & Drugs Abuse in Pakistani HEIs
World Health Organization defines drug abuse as harmful or hazardous use of psychoactive
substances, including alcohol and illicit drugs. UNODC defines “abuse” as any consumption of a
controlled substance no matter how frequent. Whereas, economic cost studies refer to “Abuse” as
any use which involves social cost to the community in addition to the cost of provision of the
drug.
As per national census of 20173, Pakistan is the sixth most populous country with a
population of 207.7 million. About 29% of the population lies in the cohort of 15-29 age group
due to which, the role of the educational institution to curb the menace of smoking and drug abuse
becomes significant.
There are a total of 210 public and private sector HEIs in Pakistan4 along with 227 sub
campus and constituent colleges with a total enrollment of 1.84 million5 students in these HEIs. It
is a dilemma of the modern world that we observe a cultural acceptance towards smoking tobacco
despite it being hazardous for the health of the smokers and for anyone breathing the smoke
contents while being around the smoker. In Pakistan, in 2017, about 163,360 people died due to
tobacco use6, 5000 Pakistanis were admitted to hospitals every day because of tobacco7. 39% of
households are exposed daily to passive tobacco smoke8. Drug abuse too has become so common
that it is no longer taboo amongst our youth.  The exact data regarding the percentage of students

conflicting, yet it is evident that the usage of drugs in higher educational institutions in Pakistan is
on rise. Factors contributing towards drug abuse in HEIs in Pakistan are:

## Anti Drug Policy For Higher Education Institutions In Pakistan — 3. Scope
It is the need of the hour to form certain guidelines in order to ensure a uniformity in drug
abuse prevention in all the HEIs of the country. The guidelines in this policy apply to the students,
faculty, staff and the visitors (including individuals associated with outsourced services) in the
premises (campus, class rooms, hostels, play grounds, libraries, laboratories, cafeterias &
university transport etc.) of the campus in all public and private sector HEIs of Pakistan.
9 News Bulletin, Annual Issue 2018, Ministry of Narcotics Control, Pakistan.

In this regard, an extended collaboration of all stake holders i.e. HEIs, Anti-Narcotics Force
(ANF), Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs), Rehabilitation Centers for drug dependents and the
parents/guardians of the students is required. This policy will provide the basic guideline to the
HEIs in ensuring a smoke and drug free environment.

## Anti Drug Policy For Higher Education Institutions In Pakistan — 4. Role of Higher Education Institutions
Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) of a country perform a key role in the edifice of the
zeitgeist. It is through these institutions that the perspective of a generation is constructed and
propagated, therefore, the HEIs have remained to be a priority for the development of any society
and nation. By raising awareness regarding the prevalent social vices amongst the youth in the
HEIs and by sensitizing them, the objective of setting our country free from the shackles of drug
addiction can be achieved.
The HIEs of Pakistan need to ensure that no stone is left unturned in the effort to eradicate
the drug abuse menace amongst the youth that are enrolled in these institutions. For this purpose,
the HEIs should take the following measures to effectively exterminate the culture of smoking and
drug abuse.
4.1. Anti-Drug Committee in HEIs
In order to control the smoking and drug abuse culture, an organized effort is required. For
this purpose, the HEIs around the country would constitute a committee to be called as “Anti-Drug
Committee” consisting of a minimum of three members, which would be duly notified by the Vice
Chancellor or Head of the Institution. The composition of the committee should be as follows:
i. 
A minimum of two regular Faculty members of BPS-18/19 and one member from
Administration office. It is also recommended that Medical Officer/Medical Practitioner (in
case employed at the University) may also be made part of the Committee.
ii.

case employed at the University) may also be made part of the Committee.
ii. 
Committee to be headed by Director Student Affairs/ Registrar or a senior faculty member
(not below grade 19).
iii. 
Keeping in view, the nature of the case being reported and investigated, the committee may
co-opt another member to assist or opine upon the issue.
iv. 
Each sub-campus of the HEI would also establish its own sub-committee constituted on a
similar pattern to perform similar duties.
